question:
Which FC mode is the device MDS-9148S-2 operating in?
MDS-9148S-2# show interface port-channel 2
port-channel 2 is up
  Hardware is Fibre Channel
  Port WWN is 24:02:8c:60:4f:2d:de:c0
  Admin port mode is NP, trunk mode is off
  snmp link state traps are enabled
  Port mode is NP
  Port vsan is 11
  Speed is 16 Gbps
  1 minute input rate 0 bits/sec, 0 bytes/sec, 0 frames/sec
  1 minute output rate 0 bits/sec, 0 bytes/sec, 0 frames/sec
    1160983754 frames input, 140497639680 bytes
    0 discards, 0 errors
    0 CRC, 0 unknown class
    0 too long, 0 too short
    90139726 frames output, 8743553423232 bytes
theory: An interface (or port channel) whose 'Admin port mode is NP' and 'Port mode is NP' is functioning as an NP (proxy N) port - the uplink type a Cisco MDS switch running NPV mode uses toward its upstream NPIV-enabled core switch. Since this port channel is up and operating in NP mode rather than F, E, or TE, MDS-9148S-2 must be an NPV edge switch relaying FLOGIs from its downstream devices through this uplink, so the switch is operating in NPV mode. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
